# Verifying a skill change (`.discobox/skills`, `.agents/skills`)
-name: Task
-description: Run one Taskfile target in the repository's Nix devShell.
-# The whole GitHub Actions layer, in one place (ADR 0066 §2). A job that needs a
-# new check gets a Taskfile target and four lines of YAML; nothing about *what*
-# the check does lives in this directory.
-# The one thing this cannot do that ADR 0066 §2 describes is check out the
-# repository: a local composite action is only resolvable once the repository is
-# already on disk, so every job runs actions/checkout first. A job that needs a
-# second target adds a plain `run: nix develop -c go tool task <target>` step —
-# Nix is already installed by then.
-inputs:
-  target:
-    description: The Taskfile target to run.
-    required: true
-runs:
-  using: composite
-  steps:
-    - name: Install Nix
-      uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31.11.1
-      with:
-        extra_nix_config: |
-          experimental-features = nix-command flakes
-    # The devShell itself comes from cache.nixos.org. This is the Go build and
-    # module cache, which is what actually dominates a check or test job.
-    # Deliberately actions/cache and not a vendor-specific one: Depot's runners
-    # back the GitHub Actions cache API with Depot Cache, so this is already the
-    # fast path there, and it still works on a GitHub-hosted runner.
-    - name: Restore the Go caches
-      uses: actions/cache@v6.1.0
-      with:
-        path: |
-          ~/.cache/go-build
-          ~/Library/Caches/go-build
-          ~/go/pkg/mod
-        # Keyed by job, not by target: a target name carries a colon, and the
-        # jobs are already one-to-one with targets. Separate keys because a
-        # cross-compiling job's cache has nothing in common with a native one's.
-        key: go-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ github.job }}-${{ hashFiles('go.work.sum', '**/go.sum') }}
-        restore-keys: |
-          go-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ github.job }}-
-          go-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
-    - name: go tool task ${{ inputs.target }}
-      shell: bash
-      run: nix develop -c go tool task ${{ inputs.target }}
-# Depot CI's half of CI, run in parallel with .github/workflows/ci.yml to
-# compare the two engines on identical work.
-# Source: .github/workflows/ci.yml, with two jobs deliberately removed.
-# Depot CI has no macOS or Windows sandboxes, so `darwin` and `windows` cannot
-# run here and are NOT copied. Leaving them in would be worse than losing them:
-# the labels would fall back to Ubuntu and both jobs would report success having
-# compiled no vz cgo, signed nothing, and exercised neither the named-pipe
-# transport nor ConPTY — the false green ADR 0066 §4 exists to prevent. Those
-# two stay on GitHub Actions, where Depot's managed runners do provide both.
-# release.yml and vm-image.yml are not migrated at all: both systems run
-# migrated workflows, so every tag would publish twice.
-# Changes made by `depot ci migrate`:
-# - Rewrote .github/ path references to .depot/
-# Every job body is one Taskfile target (ADR 0066 §1). What each target does
-# lives in Taskfile.yml and runs the same way in a terminal.
-name: CI
-# Runners are Depot's. The sizes below match what the GitHub-hosted equivalents
-# gave us (4 CPU / 16 GB) rather than Depot's 2-CPU default; raise the suffix to
-# -8 or -16 to trade money for wall-clock. Depot runners also back the GitHub
-# Actions cache API with Depot Cache, so the actions/cache in .depot/actions/task
-# is transparently ~10x faster here with no change to it.
-on:
-  pull_request:
-  push:
-    branches:
-      - main
-permissions:
-  contents: read
-concurrency:
-  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
-  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
-jobs:
-  check:
-    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
-    timeout-minutes: 30
-    steps:
-      - uses: actions/checkout@v6.0.2
-      - uses: ./.depot/actions/task
-        with:
-          target: ci:check
-  test:
-    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
-    timeout-minutes: 30
-    steps:
-      - uses: actions/checkout@v6.0.2
-      - uses: ./.depot/actions/task
-        with:
-          target: ci:test
-  verify:
-    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
-    timeout-minutes: 30
-    steps:
-      - uses: actions/checkout@v6.0.2
-      - uses: ./.depot/actions/task
-        with:
-          target: verify
-  # The release artifacts, built on every change rather than only at tag time.
-  # The Dagger release module rotted for months precisely because nothing but a
-  # tag exercised it (ADR 0066 Context).
-  build:
-    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
-    timeout-minutes: 30
-    steps:
-      - uses: actions/checkout@v6.0.2
-      - uses: ./.depot/actions/task
-        with:
-          target: release:build

- push-main: Push the current work to discobox `main` on GitHub, watch the CI run, fix whatever fails, and repeat until the pushed commit is green. Use when the user wants to push to main, get main green, or drive CI to passing.
- release: Cut a discobox release — infer the next version, get main green, tag it, watch the release workflow, and land it on the dev Homebrew channel; separately, mark an already-cut release stable so it reaches `brew install discobox`, and submit it to winget by hand. Use when the user wants to tag, release, ship a version, push a formula to the tap, promote or mark a release stable, or submit a version to winget.
- verify-recipes: This repository's recipes for verifying a change at runtime inside a discobox — a CLI or console (TUI) change against the running `task dev` loop (opening the console in an isolated tmux, signalling it, forcing a real out-of-memory kill), the nested-Docker runc wrapper (runcca / sandbox-agent/cmd/discobox-runc) via docker run and kind, the pool proxy (`proxy/`) by driving traffic from a box of the dev pool, and a change to a skill (`.discobox/skills`, `.agents/skills`) via a headless agent in an isolated HOME. Inside a discobox, the generic `verify` skill (from `.discobox/skills/verify`) reads it first and records what it learns here; outside one, Claude Code's built-in `/verify` does not know this name. Use when verifying a change to the discobox console, its terminal guard, anything reached from bare `./build/discobox`, the runc wrapper, the pool proxy, or a skill.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run shellcheck over every shell script in the working tree.
#
# A shell script is a file named *.sh, *.bash, or *.bats, one whose first line
# is a sh or bash shebang (the image's extensionless helpers, such as
# sandbox-agent/image/harness-run), or .envrc. Files sourced rather than run
# have no shebang and say which shell they are with a `# shellcheck shell=`
# directive instead.
#
# The whole tree is checked every time rather than the changed files: it takes a
# couple of seconds, and a hook that checks only what changed cannot report a
# failure it saw earlier as fixed.
#
# Inline scripts in Taskfile.yml and the Dockerfiles' RUN steps are not
# reached; shellcheck reads files, not YAML or Dockerfiles.
#
# Called by `go tool task check:shell` and by the hook of the same name.

set -euo pipefail

cd "${DISCOBOX_WORKSPACE:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"

# The working tree rather than the index: a script the hook fires on is usually
# one nobody has `git add`ed yet, and a tracked one deleted but not yet staged
# is still in the index. Ignored files stay out either way.
{
	git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -- '*.sh' '*.bash' '*.bats' .envrc
	# -n prefixes each match with its line number; only a match on line 1 is a
	# shebang. The extensions above are left out so nothing is listed twice.
	# git grep exits 1 when nothing matches, which is not a failure here.

fix(proxy): size an open audit spool through its own handle

The budget pass read every spool's size from the directory listing. Windows
updates a listed file's size only when the writer's handle closes, so an
open spool counted as empty there: the pass under-reported the spool bytes
and TestBudgetLeavesOpenSpoolsAlone and
TestBudgetDoesNotDeleteToMakeRoomForAnOpenSpool failed on the windows
runner. An open spool is now sized by opening it and statting the handle,
which reports the bytes written so far on every platform.

`main` is green: `upstream/main` is at `eff8862d`, and all six CI jobs passed for that commit in run [37817606862](https://github.com/discobox-ai/discobox/actions/runs/37817606862).

**What happened along the way:**
- **Remote name:** in this checkout the GitHub remote is `origin`; there is no `upstream`.
- **First rebase:** upstream had moved ahead by 6 commits. One file conflicted, `.agents/skills/verify-recipes/SKILL.md`: two sessions had each written a "verify the proxy without a dev pool" recipe. I merged them into one entry that keeps both methods (the plain-HTTP bridge, and the mTLS `ControlHandler` for audit and cache testing) plus the note on what makes a blob cacheable.
- **Local CI targets:** `ci:test`, `ci:check` and `verify` all passed. `ci:check` only passed once I ran it inside `nix develop`, because `shellcheck` comes from the flake and wasn't on this shell's PATH.
- **Push:** the push was rejected because a new commit had landed upstream (`1597f368`, an ADR fix). My six commits were already under it with the same SHAs, apparently pushed from another checkout that shares this `.git`. So `1597f368` became the commit to get green.
- **CI failure on `1597f368`:** only the `windows` job failed. `TestBudgetLeavesOpenSpoolsAlone` and `TestBudgetDoesNotDeleteToMakeRoomForAnOpenSpool` failed because the budget pass read file sizes from the directory listing. Windows only updates a file's listed size when the writer closes it, so a spool still being written counted as empty.
- **Fix, `eff8862d` (`fix(proxy): size an open audit spool through its own handle`):** a spool that's still open now gets its size by opening the file and checking the size through that handle, which is accurate on every platform. I couldn't run Windows here, so the passing `windows` job is the confirmation.

**Still open:**
- **`go-lsp` hook:** `check-hooks` still reports this one failing, and I pushed with it red. It flags js/wasm build errors in `cli/`, for example an unknown `websocket.DialOptions.HTTPClient` field and an undefined `syscall.SIGHUP`. My changes don't touch that code and CI doesn't build that target, but you may want to look at it.
- **Leftover file:** `wnb-build-failed.sync-conflict-…txt`, a Syncthing conflict file, is still in the working tree. I didn't commit it.

content: You asked me to push your work to main and get CI passing. That's done: commit eff8862d passed all six jobs after I fixed a Windows-only test failure. Next, look into the failing go-lsp hook in cli/. (disable recaps in /config)
